stances.claim: BBM's Cabinet nominees deserve public appreciation and recognition. The political-camp loyalists (Duterte-Carpio, Rodriguez, Abalos, Remulla, Ople, Cruz-Angeles, Lagdameo) 'are qualified and should be given the chance to show their worth in helping the President-elect unify our people and fulfill their aspirations.'

Justice secretary Remulla has been denounced for 'atrocious track record of shameless apologia for Red-tagging, human rights violations, and attacks on press freedom' -- but 'that was his stance as a partisan member of the legislative branch. Now, let us cautiously accord him the opportunity to become a statesman as the dispenser of justice in the executive branch.'

BBM's technocrats -- Diokno (finance, former Bangko Sentral governor), Balisacan (NEDA), Pascual (trade, former UP president), Bonoan (public works, ex-San Miguel), Laguesma (labor) -- 'have undeniable experience and expertise in their respective fields. I believe BBM chose them because they are respected professionals, not political wannabees.' Diokno, Balisacan, Pascual, and Medalla (the incoming Bangko Sentral governor) are 'brilliant UP grads' -- 'On their robust shoulders rests our people's hope for better lives.'

Sen. Grace Poe's vindication was institutionally complete: 'a foundling left in a church in Iloilo' won decisively before the SC by 9-3-3 to uphold her natural-born-citizen status (CJ supported her plea unequivocally in 2015-2016 columns) -- and she did not stop at her own victory but sponsored RA 11767 (signed last week) extending the protection to all foundlings 'from the moment of birth.'

Justice Maria Filomena D. Singh (55) was 'fittingly elevated' to the seat vacated by SAJ Estela M. Perlas-Bernabe -- climbing the four judicial-ladder rungs (QC MeTC → QC RTC → CA → SC) like her predecessor, who had inherited the seat from another career lady jurist, Conchita Carpio-Morales. Singh is 'unpredictable' with 'no backlog since she started her judicial calling,' and has 'more than a fair chance of becoming another SAJ (or even a chief justice)' along with 55-year-old peers Hernando, Marquez, and Kho.

Pattern observation: Singh's Ateneo law degree preserves Ateneo dominance on the SC (6 of 15 members, 7 with the Ateneo de Davao grad), while UP's UP College of Law has only 2 members -- but 'Ateneo dominates the Supreme Court but UP sways the BBM economic team.' A clean institutional-pedigree divide between high court and economic command.

Singh is the first female professorial-chair holder in law of the Metrobank Foundation, having delivered her first lecture March 5, 2021 at the SC Session Hall while still an appellate justice -- CJ vows to monitor her career and her fidelity to 'proven competence, integrity, probity, and independence' 'as long as the Good Lord would allow me.'

notable_anecdotes: Remulla's 'atrocious track record of shameless apologia for Red-tagging, human rights violations, and attacks on press freedom' -- quoted as denunciation -- paired with CJ's provisional-trust framing ('let us cautiously accord him the opportunity to become a statesman'). A textbook case of CJ's criticism-acknowledgment-with-civic-charity register.

Grace Poe identified as 'a foundling left in a church in Iloilo' -- preserved as the most poignant biographical fact and the source of the constitutional question that nearly disqualified her from senatorship and the presidency. The 9-3-3 SC vindication is then extended legislatively to all foundlings via RA 11767.

Justice Singh's career arc -- climbing all four judicial-ladder rungs (QC MeTC, QC RTC, CA, SC) -- same path as Perlas-Bernabe before her, who inherited from Conchita Carpio-Morales, building 'eminent career lady jurist' lineage.
The Ateneo-UP school-pedigree epigram -- 'Ateneo dominates the Supreme Court but UP sways the BBM economic team' -- a quotable institutional pattern.

CJ's signature humility closing: 'I intend to monitor her Supreme Court career and her fidelity to the constitutional ideals of proven competence, integrity, probity, and independence as long as the Good Lord would allow me.' -- the 'as long as the Good Lord would allow me' as recurring CJ voicemark.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban offers three appreciations of BBM transition figures. First, on the Cabinet: while many appointees came from BBM's political camp (VP Sara Duterte-Carpio at education; Victor Rodriguez as executive secretary; Benhur Abalos at DILG; Jesus Crispin Remulla at justice; Susan Ople at migrant workers; Trixie Cruz-Angeles at press; Anton Lagdameo as special assistant), they 'are qualified and should be given the chance to show their worth.' Remulla has been denounced for 'atrocious track record of shameless apologia for Red-tagging, human rights violations, and attacks on press freedom,' but that was 'his stance as a partisan member of the legislative branch. Now, let us cautiously accord him the opportunity to become a statesman as the dispenser of justice in the executive branch.' BBM's technocrats -- 'the indefatigable' Benjamin Diokno (finance, former Bangko Sentral governor, who has already announced retention of national treasurer Lea de Leon and current finance undersecretaries including 'capable lawyer-CPA' Antonette Tionko), 'economic guru' Arsenio Balisacan (NEDA), former UP president Alfredo Pascual (trade), San Miguel Corp executive Manuel Bonoan (public works), Bienvenido Laguesma (labor), and 'impeccable banker' Felipe Medalla replacing Diokno at Bangko Sentral -- were chosen 'because they are respected professionals, not political wannabees.' Diokno, Balisacan, Pascual, and Medalla are all 'brilliant UP grads -- On their robust shoulders rests our people's hope for better lives.' Second, on Sen. Grace Poe: 'a foundling left in a church in Iloilo,' she 'won decisively in the Supreme Court that definitively upheld, by a vote of 9-3-3, her status as a natural-born citizen of her beloved Philippines' (CJ supported her plea in several 2015-2016 columns), and she did not stop at her own victory -- 'tirelessly labored' to sponsor Republic Act No. 11767 (signed last week) extending the protection to all foundlings 'from the moment of birth.' Third, on Justice Maria Filomena D. Singh (55), 'fittingly elevated' to the seat vacated by Senior AJ Estela M. Perlas-Bernabe: like Perlas-Bernabe before her (who in turn inherited the seat from 'another eminent career lady jurist, Conchita Carpio-Morales'), Singh climbed all four judicial-ladder rungs (QC MeTC → QC RTC → CA → SC). She is 'unpredictable' with 'no backlog since she started her judicial calling,' and has 'more than a fair chance of becoming another SAJ (or even a chief justice)' along with 55-year-old peers Hernando, Marquez, and Kho. Like Perlas-Bernabe, she is an Ateneo de Manila law graduate -- preserving Ateneo dominance on the SC at 6 of 15 (7 with the Ateneo de Davao grad), while UP has only 2 members. CJ's epigram: 'Ateneo dominates the Supreme Court but UP sways the BBM economic team.' Singh is also the first female professorial chair holder in law of the Metrobank Foundation, having delivered her first lecture March 5, 2021 at the SC Session Hall while still an appellate justice. CJ vows to monitor her career and 'her fidelity to the constitutional ideals of proven competence, integrity, probity, and independence as long as the Good Lord would allow me.'
